name: York Retreat moral treatment
description: The York Retreat opened in 1796 for members of the Society of Friends with mental illness and became associated with an approach known as moral treatment.

impact.note: One institution whose humane regime improved existing asylum care and was copied by asylums in Britain and North America, scored low as a single site.

date.label: 1796 CE
date.basis: Date reported by the cited source.

events.statement: The York Retreat opened in 1796 for members of the Society of Friends with mental illness; its care became associated with moral treatment.
events.caveats: An institutional historical care model, not evidence of clinical effectiveness, voluntary admission, or a universal standard of humane care. Other mental-health traditions existed earlier. The museum dates the institution’s opening, but does not demonstrate that all features of the later-described approach were present from that day.

evidence.supports: The museum dates the opening to 1796 and describes the Friends institution and later spread of its moral treatment approach.
